Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights — redlines (MSA Section: Audit & Inspection)

Claire — following up with lean redlines and rationale. I’ve included the key proposed edits inline below and attached a PDF with full page-level redlines. High-level summary first:

- SOC 2: Redwood confirms annual SOC 2 Type II coverage for the hosted environment used by Evergreen. We will provide a redacted report within 30 days of request. Redactions limited to customer-identifying details and third-party vendor attachments.
- Pen test / ad-hoc testing: We can accommodate one customer-initiated pen test per 12-month period with 30 days advance notice; additional ad-hoc tests are permitted subject to mutual agreement. Redwood requires tests to be non-destructive, follow our safety checklist (see attached playbook), and coordinate with SRE to define IP ranges and test windows.
- On-prem inspections: To balance operational risk, on-site inspections will be replaced by vendor-assisted evidence exchange (secure share of logs, configuration snapshots) unless there is a narrow, documented need and a separate statement of work.
- Evidence cadence: Redwood will provide monthly extracts for access logs and system health summaries for a rolling 90-day window. Full historical retention requests (beyond 90 days) can be handled by the support plan / add-on.

Suggested contract language (excerpt):
"Audit & Inspection. Customer may request compliance evidence including Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report, security policies, and relevant configuration artifacts. Redwood will provide (a) a redacted SOC 2 Type II report annually and upon reasonable request; (b) monthly access log extracts in a mutually agreed format for a rolling 90-day window; and (c) a mutually scheduled, non-destructive penetration test with at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice. Any on-site inspection by Customer shall be limited to a separate statement of work and subject to Redwood’s operational safety requirements."

Rationale / negotiation points we expect:
- We can deliver SOC2 Type II and monthly extracts, but we cannot support unlimited on-prem audits or unbounded historical log exports without a commercial add-on.
- For pen tests we need to limit scope to non-production-impacting activities and require a signed testing agreement (we included a one-page testing checklist in the pen test playbook).

Attached: redlines_MSA_section_8_Audit_and_Inspection.pdf and pen_test_playbook.pdf.

I’ll make the redline PDF editable if your GC wants track-changes; otherwise Jordan can surface next steps.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Laura — thank you for the clear edit and the language excerpt. A few clarifications from our GC and security team after reviewing your PDF:

1) SOC 2 cadence: we require evidence within 14 days of a procurement request. Would Redwood commit to providing the latest redacted Type II report within 14 days instead of 30? Our GC marked this as material.
2) Evidence cadence (monthly extracts): acceptable, but for certain controlled data flows our auditors want a quarterly bundle of system-config snapshots retained for 12 months — is that feasible as an add-on?
3) Pen test frequency: could we instead specify "one (1) customer-initiated penetration test per 12-month period plus one additional test following any major platform upgrade"? That would cover our needs operationally.

We uploaded a completed questionnaire (Evergreen_Security_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx) with the fields we need filled for procurement — can you confirm who will populate the vendor answers?

If we can agree to the SOC 2 14-day window and the pen test frequency language above, GC is prepared to accept the proposed limit on on-site inspections and move to commercial review.

–Claire

Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights — operational clarifications (pen test + logs)

Claire — quick operational notes from SRE side to align expectations:

- Pen test windows: we prefer scheduled maintenance windows (we can offer a weekday evening UTC window) to minimize impact. Production-impacting tests require explicit sign-off and a separate SOW.
- IP ranges and scope: we will provide a set of IP blocks and an allowlist for active testing. Any external scanning outside that list requires prior coordination.
- Test method: Redwood supports application-layer and authenticated tests. For tests that need deeper access to infrastructure we require a test harness in a mapped staging environment.
- Evidence extracts: monthly access logs are available as CSV exports; we can automate delivery to a secure S3 bucket. Historical retention beyond 90 days will be an add-on; we can propose a 12-month retention bundle in pricing.

I attached our pen test playbook — it contains the checklist, approved test types, and the standard ephemeral credentials workflow (expiration 8 hours). If Evergreen is OK with the 14-day SOC2 turnaround request from Legal, Redwood will commit to prioritizing the procurement channel so the report is available within that window.

Happy to set a short technical sync to finalize IP ranges and the testing checklist.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability (CS/SRE), Redwood Inference
